content:
# Refactor Plan: `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py`

**Scope of this phase:** test specification and decomposition ordering only.
No code, no tests, no module split written. This plan is downstream of the
coverage-gate verdict, reproduced below because it governs everything that
follows.

## Verdict inherited from the coverage gate

> **CHARACTERIZATION TESTS REQUIRED FIRST**

Under `-m unit` — the marker set CI actually gates on — `_wiring.py` sits at
40% coverage, and the 60% that's missing is not evenly distributed: it is
concentrated exactly in the highest-consequence code in the file (every
ADR-060 fallback chain, the entire prompt-assembly pipeline, the singleton
identity/reset contracts). The pure command-builder surface is genuinely
well-pinned. Nothing else is. This plan's job is to specify the tests that
close that gap, in the order that lets decomposition proceed safely instead
of as a single 40-test pre-step nobody finishes.

---

## 1. What the module owns (target decomposition)

`_wiring.py` is a composition root: a `main.py`-style file whose job is side
effects at construction time (instantiate adapters, wire handlers, hold
process-lifetime singletons), not a library of pure functions. The 1582
lines break into seven ownership clusters that already exist as de facto
seams in the current file (see its own section comments — "Phase 3
additions", "Claude plugin injection (issue #726)", "Skill wiring (issue
#772)"). The proposed target module layout, one file per cluster:

| New module | Owns | Current lines (approx) |
|---|---|---|
| `_wiring/commands.py` | `_build_claude_command`, `_build_codex_command`, `_is_codex_model`, `_build_agent_command`, `apply_tool_policy_to_prompt`, `UnsupportedToolPolicyError`, `_CLAUDE_MODEL_ALIASES` | 254-436 |
| `_wiring/prompts.py` | `_owner_repo_from_url`, `_substitute_builtins`, `_substitute_inputs`, `_build_context_appendix`, `_build_workspace_prompt` | 439-542 |
| `_wiring/dedup.py` | `_create_dedup_adapter`, `_create_import_ledger`, `get_pending_sha_store`, their three singleton globals | 621-838 |
| `_wiring/event_pipeline.py` | `get_event_pipeline`, `get_webhook_health_tracker`, `get_trigger_repo`/`get_trigger_store`, `_InMemoryAggregateRepository`, `_test_trigger_repo` | 593-780 |
| `_wiring/execution.py` | `get_execution_processor`, `get_execute_workflow_handler`, `get_workflow_dispatcher`, `BackgroundWorkflowDispatcher`, `_NullSignalQueueAdapter`, `get_controller`, `_build_session_store`, `_build_workspace_telemetry_env` | 129-251, 869-1055 |
| `_wiring/claude_plugins.py` | Everything in the "Claude plugin injection (issue #726)" block, `reset_claude_plugin_singletons` | 1193-1474 |
| `_wiring/skills.py` | Everything in the "Skill wiring (issue #772)" block, `reset_skill_singletons` | 1476-1583 |
| `_wiring/__init__.py` (or a slimmed `_wiring.py`) | `ensure_connected`, `disconnect`, `get_projection_mgr`, the read-only query getters (`get_session_cost_query`, `get_execution_cost_query`, `get_canonical_usage_query`, `get_conversation_store`, `get_realtime`, `get_subscription_coordinator`, `_get_budget_checker`, `get_github_settings`, thin repo/publisher getters), re-exports for backward-compatible imports | remainder |

This is a **move**, not a **rewrite**. No cluster's internal logic changes;
only import locations and (per §4) two seams get an injected collaborator
instead of a hardcoded lookup. Every existing external import of
`syn_api._wiring.X` must keep working — either by re-exporting from the
package `__init__.py`, or by a follow-up commit updating call sites, decided
per-step below.

## 2. Why characterization tests are the gating dependency, not a nice-to-have

The coverage gate already named the mechanism: `_create_dedup_adapter`,
`_create_import_ledger`, and `get_pending_sha_store` are the three largest
functions in the file by branch count, they are also the three most likely
to get "simplified" by an agent doing a decomposition pass (their
Postgres/Redis/in-memory/raise shape is repetitive-looking, which is exactly
what invites consolidation into a shared helper), and none of their branches
run under the CI-gated suite. A refactor that quietly collapses "Redis
unavailable → raise" and "Postgres pool None → try Redis" into one shared
`try/except` would pass every existing test and reintroduce the silent
in-memory fallback ADR-060 exists to forbid. The same applies to prompt
assembly: it's the widest-blast-radius code in the file (every phase of
every workflow execution goes through it) and has a duplicate-logic decoy
test (`test_cc_command_features.py::TestArgumentsSubstitution`) that would
stay green regardless of what happens to the real function — so today,
*nothing* would turn red if this cluster's move introduced a substitution
bug.

---

## 3. Characterization test specification

Each entry: the exact behaviour pinned, inputs → observable result, why it
breaks under the specific extraction move, and the test level with
justification for not going cheaper.

### 3.1 `_create_dedup_adapter` (lines 656-706) — gates the `dedup.py` extraction

**CT-1: in-memory mode returns `InMemoryDedupAdapter`, no I/O attempted.**
- Input: `get_settings()` mocked so `uses_in_memory_stores` is `True`.
- Result: `isinstance(result, InMemoryDedupAdapter)`; no attempt to import
  `syn_api._wiring_db` or `redis.asyncio` (assert via `monkeypatch` sentinels
  that raise if touched, or via `mocker.patch` call-count 0).
- Breaks under: moving this function into a new module can reorder the
  early-return check relative to the settings read, or the module-split
  script can "helpfully" hoist the `get_settings()` import to module level —
  which breaks the deliberate late-import pattern the file uses everywhere
  to avoid import-time settings resolution in tests.
- Level: **unit**. No real Postgres/Redis touched; the branch selection is
  pure given a settings double.

**CT-2: Postgres path selected when `syn_observability_db_url` is set and
the shared pool is non-None.**
- Input: settings double with `uses_in_memory_stores=False`,
  `syn_observability_db_url="postgres://..."`; monkeypatch
  `syn_api._wiring_db.get_shared_db_pool` to return a sentinel pool object.
- Result: `isinstance(result, PostgresDedupAdapter)`; the adapter's `ttl_days`
  equals `max(1, -(-settings.polling.dedup_ttl_seconds // 86400))` for at
  least two `dedup_ttl_seconds` values that straddle a day boundary (e.g.
  `86400` → `1`, `86401` → `2`) — this is a ceiling-division formula, easy to
  get subtly wrong (off-by-one) if rewritten during extraction, and nothing
  currently asserts it.
- Breaks under: extraction that changes how `get_shared_db_pool` is imported
  (currently a local import inside the function, which is what makes it
  monkeypatchable per-test) to a module-level import — the test becomes
  unable to inject the sentinel pool, silently reducing this test's coverage
  to "always exercises the real global."
- Level: **unit** with a fake pool object (not a real asyncpg pool — this
  function never awaits anything on the pool, it just passes it through).

**CT-3: Postgres configured but pool construction raises → falls through to
Redis, not to the caller.**
- Input: `syn_observability_db_url` set; `get_shared_db_pool` monkeypatched
  to raise (simulating the `try/except Exception` at line 672-686); Redis
  reachable (`redis.asyncio.from_url` monkeypatched to a sentinel client).
- Result: `isinstance(result, RedisDedupAdapter)`, not a raised exception.
- Breaks under: the exact anti-pattern named in §2 — collapsing the two
  `try/except` blocks (682 and 699) into one during a "these look similar"
  cleanup pass changes which failure lands in the RuntimeError branch.
- Level: **unit**. This is specifically the fallthrough-on-exception behavior,
  which is untestable at a cheaper level than forcing the exception.

**CT-4: Postgres unset, Redis unreachable → raises `RuntimeError` naming
ADR-060, does NOT return an in-memory adapter.**
- Input: `syn_observability_db_url=None` (or pool None), and
  `redis.asyncio.from_url` (or the whole `import redis.asyncio` at line 689)
  monkeypatched to raise.
- Result: `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="ADR-060")`. This is the single
  most important assertion in the whole spec: it is the fail-loudly contract
  the entire module exists to enforce, and it is currently exercised by
  **zero tests** under either coverage measurement in the gate report.
- Breaks under: any refactor that adds a "just in case" in-memory fallback
  to the final `except` clause — the failure mode is silent (tests pass,
  production loses dedup durability on restart) unless this exact path is
  forced.
- Level: **unit**. Forcing both a Postgres and a Redis failure in the same
  test needs no real network; a level-appropriate level would be
  slower without adding confidence (integration tests using a real
  unreachable Redis URL would just be this test with more latency).

### 3.2 `_create_import_ledger` (lines 712-761) — gates `dedup.py`, singleton-aware

**CT-5: singleton short-circuit — second call returns the SAME object,
does not re-read settings.**
- Input: call `_create_import_ledger()` twice with in-memory settings between
  calls; spy on `get_settings` call count.
- Result: `result_1 is result_2`; `get_settings` called once, not twice
  (first call caches into `_import_ledger_singleton` at line 731-733, the
  guard runs before any settings read).
- Breaks under: extraction that moves the module-level `_import_ledger_singleton`
  global without moving its `global` statement into the same module as the
  function that mutates it — a copy-paste split that leaves the getter in
  one file and the global in another silently creates two independent
  "singletons" that never converge, defeating the whole point (the docstring
  at 715-719 explains WHY this must be one instance: a fresh Postgres adapter
  per dispatch re-issues `CREATE TABLE`, and a fresh in-memory one forgets the
  cross-phase mark — reintroducing #936).
- Level: **unit**. Object identity is a language-level property; no I/O
  needed to observe it.

**CT-6: production with no `SYN_OBSERVABILITY_DB_URL` raises `RuntimeError`
mentioning `#936` — no Redis tier exists for this one (unlike dedup).**
- Input: `uses_in_memory_stores=False`, `syn_observability_db_url=None`.
- Result: `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="936")`.
- Breaks under: a refactor that generalizes `_create_dedup_adapter` and
  `_create_import_ledger` into one shared "try Postgres, try Redis, raise"
  helper — plausible-looking because they have near-identical shape, but the
  docstring at 721-725 is explicit that there is deliberately NO Redis tier
  here (a ledger in a different store than the cost rows it must agree with
  is worse than no ledger). A shared helper would silently add one.
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-7: Postgres path returns `PostgresImportLedger`, and the singleton
persists it — a second call after a raise-then-fix does not re-attempt
construction.**
- Input: settings with `syn_observability_db_url` set, `get_shared_db_pool`
  returning a sentinel pool.
- Result: `isinstance(result, PostgresImportLedger)`; identity-stable across
  repeat calls per CT-5.
- Level: **unit**.

### 3.3 `get_pending_sha_store` (lines 789-837) — gates `dedup.py`

Same three-branch shape as `_create_dedup_adapter` minus the Redis tier —
Postgres or raise, wrapped in a singleton.

**CT-8: in-memory mode caches `InMemoryPendingSHAStore` in the singleton.**
Mirrors CT-1 + CT-5 combined (branch selection + identity stability).
Level: **unit**.

**CT-9: Postgres pool construction raising falls through to the
`RuntimeError`, not silently returning `None` or an unguarded adapter.**
- Input: `syn_observability_db_url` set, `get_shared_db_pool` monkeypatched to
  raise inside the `try` at line 813-830.
- Result: `pytest.raises(RuntimeError)` — the `except Exception: logger.warning(...)`
  at 826-830 must fall through to the raise at 833-837, not swallow it.
- Breaks under: a refactor that "cleans up" the duplicate `except Exception:
  logger.warning(...)` blocks shared across all three ADR-060 functions into
  one decorator/helper — easy to get the control flow wrong (e.g. `return
  None` instead of falling through to raise) since the three functions'
  post-except behavior actually differs (dedup falls through to a THIRD
  tier; this one and the ledger fall through directly to raise).
- Level: **unit**.

### 3.4 `get_controller` (lines 872-918) — gates `execution.py`

**CT-10: Redis reachable → `RedisSignalQueueAdapter`; Redis unreachable →
`_NullSignalQueueAdapter`, and construction does NOT raise either way.**
- Input: two settings/monkeypatch variants for `redis.asyncio.from_url`
  (success and raise).
- Result: type of `signal_adapter` differs; in BOTH cases `get_controller()`
  returns a valid `ExecutionController`, never propagates the Redis
  exception. This is notably a *different* failure posture from the dedup
  functions (degrade to null adapter, not fail loudly) — worth pinning
  explicitly so a refactor doesn't "fix" the inconsistency by making this one
  raise too, which would take down pause/resume/cancel for a reason unrelated
  to ADR-060 (this isn't durable state, it's a live signal queue).
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-11: singleton identity — second call returns the same
`ExecutionController` instance regardless of Redis state at the second call.**
Mirrors CT-5. This one matters because `get_execution_processor` wires
`controller=get_controller()` directly (line 242) — an extraction that
breaks the singleton means the processor and any route calling
`get_controller()` independently would get different signal queues,
silently breaking pause/resume.
Level: **unit**.

### 3.5 Prompt-assembly pipeline (lines 439-542) — gates `prompts.py`, highest priority per the gate

**CT-12: `_substitute_builtins` replaces all three built-ins, and leaves
`{{repository}}` untouched when the template doesn't use it (no spurious
warning log).**
- Input: template `"exec={{execution_id}} wf={{workflow_id}} repo={{repo_url}}"`,
  concrete ids/url.
- Result: exact string equality on output; `caplog` has zero warning records.
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-13: `{{repository}}` present → derives `owner/repo` from `repo_url` via
`_owner_repo_from_url` AND logs the deprecation warning naming issue #715.**
- Input: template containing `{{repository}}`, `repo_url="https://github.com/acme/widgets.git"`.
- Result: output contains `"acme/widgets"`; `caplog` warning message contains
  `"715"` and the workflow_id.
- Breaks under: this is the one branch the gate report flags as untested
  even within the "well-pinned" command-builder-adjacent cluster (464→473
  partial branch) — a move that reorders the `if` check relative to the
  three unconditional replaces above it changes nothing observably UNLESS
  this exact input is tried, which is why it's currently invisible.
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-14: `_substitute_inputs` layer ordering — workflow inputs (2a), phase
static inputs (2b), and phase-output inlining (2c) do not clobber each other
when the same key exists at more than one layer.**
- Input: template `"{{x}}"`; `inputs={"x": "from-workflow"}`; a phase whose
  `phase.inputs` contains a static input named `x` with value `"from-phase"`.
  (Whichever layer runs second — 2b runs after 2a in source order — wins;
  the test pins THAT specific precedence, not an idealized one.)
- Result: exact output string, documenting which layer's value survives.
  This is a **characterization** test in the literal sense of the brief: if
  this precedence is surprising, it is still what ships today, and the test
  says so rather than asserting what "should" happen.
- Breaks under: this is exactly the function §2 flags as having a
  hand-duplicated decoy test that omits layers 2b/2c entirely — an extraction
  is the single most likely moment for someone to "notice" the decoy, assume
  it's the real coverage, and not check layer ordering survives the move.
- Level: **unit**. No I/O; pure string transform over a constructed
  `ExecutablePhase` value object.

**CT-15: `_substitute_inputs` layer 2c — phase-output inlining truncates at
2000 chars (`content[:2000]`), and this truncation is silent (no marker,
no ellipsis).**
- Input: `phase_outputs={"phase-a": "x" * 3000}`, template `"{{phase-a}}"`.
- Result: `len(output) == 2000`; output has no `"..."` or other truncation
  marker appended — pinning that the truncation is currently silent (a
  refactor that "improves" this by adding a marker changes prompt text sent
  to every phase and belongs in a reviewed change, not an incidental
  refactor side effect).
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-16: `_substitute_inputs` layer 2d — `$ARGUMENTS` resolves from
`inputs["task"]`, defaulting to empty string, independent of whether `task`
also appears as a `{{task}}` key substituted in layer 2a.**
- Input: `inputs={"task": "do the thing"}`, template `"$ARGUMENTS"`.
- Result: `"do the thing"`. Second case: `inputs=None` → `"$ARGUMENTS"`
  resolves to `""` (line 500's `(inputs or {}).get("task", "")` default),
  not left as the literal `"$ARGUMENTS"` string.
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-17: `_build_context_appendix` — one `### Phase {id}` section per entry,
in dict iteration order, each truncated independently at 2000 chars.**
- Input: `phase_outputs` with two entries.
- Result: exact string equality including the leading
  `"\n## Context from Previous Phases"` header (line 508) — this literal text
  is sent to the model; getting the heading level or whitespace wrong during
  a move is invisible without a byte-exact assertion.
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-18 (integration): `_build_workspace_prompt` end-to-end — the four
functions compose in the documented order (builtins → inputs → task/context
prepend → appendix), against a real `ExecutablePhase` and the real
`SYN_WORKSPACE_PROMPT` constant, not a stub.**
- Input: a phase with a `prompt_template` combining a builtin
  (`{{execution_id}}`), a workflow input, and `$ARGUMENTS`; non-empty
  `phase_outputs`.
- Result: exact composed string, asserting `SYN_WORKSPACE_PROMPT` appears
  first, `## Task` section second with fully-substituted content, and the
  context appendix appears LAST only when `phase_outputs` is non-empty (the
  `if phase_outputs:` guard at line 539 — the empty-dict case must NOT
  include the appendix section at all, not include it empty).
- Breaks under: this is the function the gate calls "highest-consequence" —
  a refactor that moves `_substitute_builtins`/`_substitute_inputs` into
  `prompts.py` but leaves `_build_workspace_prompt`'s import of
  `SYN_WORKSPACE_PROMPT` (a local import at line 532, deliberately deferred)
  as a module-level import in the new file changes nothing functionally
  today, but reintroduces the exact kind of import-order fragility the file
  uses local imports everywhere to avoid. A unit test on the two helpers
  individually (CT-12 through CT-17) would NOT catch a composition-order
  bug — e.g. if the appendix got appended before the `## Task` section, each
  helper still returns correct output individually.
- Level: **integration**, specifically because "the pieces are individually
  correct but wired in the wrong order" is a composition-level failure a
  cheaper unit test cannot see by construction — this is the reason to test
  the seam that the CLUSTER BOUNDARY (prompts.py's public function)
  represents, not just its internals.

**CT-19: delete/redirect the decoy in `test_cc_command_features.py`.** Not a
new test — a removal, sequenced explicitly in §5 step 2, because the gate
report names it as actively harmful (looks like coverage, cannot detect
drift). Listed here because it is the direct payoff of CT-14/CT-18 existing:
once the real function has real coverage, the hand-duplicated
`TestArgumentsSubstitution._substitute` staticmethod has no remaining
purpose and its presence is a trap for the next reader.

### 3.6 Singleton reset contracts — gates `claude_plugins.py` / `skills.py` split

**CT-20: `reset_claude_plugin_singletons()` clears all nine module globals it
declares `global` for, verified by name, not by re-import.**
- Input: populate all nine singletons via their respective getters (using
  in-memory/test settings so no real MinIO/event-store I/O is required —
  `get_claude_plugin_storage` already branches to `get_test_claude_plugin_storage()`
  under `uses_in_memory_stores`), call `reset_claude_plugin_singletons()`,
  call each getter again.
- Result: each getter constructs a NEW object on the second call
  (`is not` the pre-reset instance) — asserted per-singleton, not just "no
  exception."
- Breaks under: this is the concrete risk the module-boundaries section of
  the gate flags explicitly — splitting the nine `global` singleton
  declarations and the reset function across module boundaries (e.g. reset
  function stays in one file, some singletons move to another) means
  `global _foo_singleton` in the reset function no longer refers to the same
  binding the getter reads, and reset becomes a silent no-op for the moved
  singletons. Python's `global` is per-module; this is invisible in a diff
  that "just moves functions."
- Level: **unit**, but MUST run against the real module namespace after
  extraction (not a mock) — this specific failure mode only manifests
  against actual module-level bindings.

**CT-21: same shape for `reset_skill_singletons()` and its four globals.**
Level: **unit**, same justification as CT-20.

**CT-22: `get_claude_plugin_lock_projection()` returns the SAME instance the
manager's `sync_published_events_to_projections` writes through — the
docstring's stated invariant ("route reads and writes must share one
instance") pinned directly rather than trusted from the comment.**
- Input: call `get_claude_plugin_lock_projection()`, then
  `get_projection_manager().get_projection("claude_plugin_lock")` directly.
- Result: `is` identity, not just equal state.
- Breaks under: an extraction that gives `claude_plugins.py` its own
  `get_projection_manager()` import path that resolves differently than the
  one `event_pipeline.py` or the manager singleton itself uses — unlikely
  with a straight move, but this is a one-line test for a documented
  invariant that currently has zero coverage, so it belongs in the
  characterization set regardless of how likely the specific break is.
- Level: **unit**. `get_projection_manager()` is itself a process-wide
  singleton factory; no real projection replay needed.

### 3.7 `_build_session_store` (lines 129-147) — gates `execution.py`

**CT-23: disabled store → `None`, no `HttpSessionStore` constructed.**
- Input: settings double, `session_store.is_enabled=False`.
- Result: `None`; spy on `HttpSessionStore.__init__` never called.
- Level: **unit**.

**CT-24: enabled store uses the READ token, not the write token, when both
exist — the exact hazard the docstring names (401-forever-retry).**
- Input: settings double with `session_store.is_enabled=True`,
  `session_store.url` set, and `effective_read_token` /
  a distinguishable write-token field both populated with different secret
  values.
- Result: the `HttpSessionStore` constructed receives the READ token's
  value as `auth_token`, asserted by inspecting the constructed instance
  (or by patching `HttpSessionStore` and asserting the kwarg it was called
  with) — NOT the write token's value.
- Breaks under: this is the exact bug the docstring warns is silent —
  "every delegate would retry forever and none would ever be priced" — a
  401 is not an exception this module raises, so no existing test would
  turn red if an extraction accidentally passed the wrong token attribute.
  Currently **zero tests** touch this function at all per the gate report.
- Level: **unit**.

### 3.8 `_build_agent_command` provider dispatch — extend existing coverage, don't duplicate it

The gate report confirms `_build_claude_command`, `_build_codex_command`,
`_build_agent_command`, and `apply_tool_policy_to_prompt` are already
genuinely pinned by `test_wiring_command_builder.py` and
`test_tool_policy_enforcement.py`. No new characterization tests are
specified for this cluster — it is the one part of the file where "extract
and move" is close to mechanically safe today. The only action item here is
**do not let the extraction touch these files' import paths without running
them** (see §5 step 1): they gate the FIRST extraction precisely because
they already exist and already pass.

### 3.9 What is explicitly NOT specified, and why

- `get_event_pipeline`, `get_execution_processor`,
  `get_execute_workflow_handler`, `get_workflow_dispatcher`,
  `get_subscription_coordinator`: these are pure composition (call N other
  factories, pass results to a constructor) with no branching logic of their
  own beyond what's already covered by testing their callees (CT-1 through
  CT-11 cover the branchy collaborators these functions call). A
  characterization test here would mostly assert "constructor was called
  with these kwargs," which is a change-detector test, not a behavior pin —
  it would fail on the extraction itself (import paths move) without
  protecting anything the callee tests don't already protect. **Exception:**
  if the extraction changes which module owns the intermediate wiring (e.g.
  `get_execution_processor` moving to `execution.py` while `_create_import_ledger`
  moves to `dedup.py`), add a single integration-level test asserting
  `get_execution_processor()` still returns a fully-constructed
  `WorkflowExecutionProcessor` with no `None` fields where a real object is
  expected — this is cheap insurance against a broken cross-module import,
  not a new behavior pin. Not listed as a numbered CT because it's
  contingent on the specific extraction PR's shape; call it out in that PR's
  description instead.
- `get_session_cost_query`, `get_execution_cost_query`,
  `get_canonical_usage_query`: identical one-branch shape (raise if
  `pool is None`, else construct). Given they're moving into the same target
  module (`__init__.py`/remainder) rather than being split apart, and their
  branch is a single `if pool is None: raise`, a move cannot silently change
  their behavior the way it can for the three-tier ADR-060 functions. Treat
  as **residual risk, not gated**: acceptable to move without a new test,
  called out explicitly per the "SAFE TO REFACTOR, smaller job" carve-out in
  the task brief for functions that are pinned only incidentally (here:
  not pinned at all, but low enough branch complexity that a move can't
  hide a behavior change the way it can in the ADR-060 trio).

---

## 4. What's genuinely NEW — TDD, not characterization

Two things in the target structure don't exist in the current file and
should be written test-first, not characterization-first, because there is
no existing behavior to pin:

**New: a `SettingsPort` Protocol (or reuse of the existing `Settings` type
directly with dependency injection) for the three ADR-060 functions.**
Currently `_create_dedup_adapter`, `_create_import_ledger`, and
`get_pending_sha_store` each do `from syn_shared.settings import get_settings;
settings = get_settings()` as their first line — a hard dependency on the
global settings singleton that is WHY CT-1 through CT-9 have to monkeypatch
`syn_shared.settings.get_settings` (module-path patching, fragile to import
reorganization) rather than injecting a fake. If the decomposition step for
`dedup.py` also introduces an explicit `settings: Settings` parameter (or a
narrower `DedupSettingsPort` with just the 3-4 fields these functions read),
that parameter's contract is NEW and should be driven test-first:
  - Write a failing test asserting `_create_dedup_adapter(settings=fake)` accepts
    an injected settings object and does NOT call `get_settings()` internally.
  - Only then change the signature.
  - This is optional scope — the decomposition works without it (§5 doesn't
    require it) — but if taken, it's TDD, and the characterization tests in
    §3.1-§3.3 should be written to work identically before and after (they
    already inject via monkeypatched `get_settings`, so switching to
    constructor injection is a signature change the characterization tests
    should catch if done carelessly — i.e., they double as the regression
    check for this migration too).

**New: whatever `__init__.py`/facade module re-exports the split symbols.**
Its only job is import compatibility. Test-first here means: before moving
a single function, write the test that imports `from syn_api._wiring import
_build_claude_command` (the CURRENT import path) and asserts it's callable
— this test should PASS before extraction (trivially, it's the current
file) and must STILL PASS after each extraction step. This isn't a
characterization test of behavior; it's a contract test of the public
import surface, and it's the one thing in this plan that should be RED
before the facade exists in its final form and GREEN after — classic TDD,
just for a module-shape contract instead of a business behavior.

Everything else in the target structure (the seven cluster files) is a
**move** of existing functions with unchanged internals — characterization-covered
per §3, not TDD.

## 5. Ordering — what gates what

The rule from the brief: each extraction step needs its net in place BEFORE
that step. Sequenced below; steps are independent enough to land as separate
PRs, each keeping `just qa-ci` green.

**Step 0 (prerequisite, not an extraction) — fix the marker gap.**
Add `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit` to `test_wiring_telemetry_env.py` and
(after auditing which of its 25 tests are true unit tests vs need
`.integration`) `test_claude_plugins_routes.py`. This is what makes "CI
stays green throughout" mean anything for this module — right now 13 points
of coverage the naive local run reports are invisible to the gate, which
means a regression in that surface during extraction would pass CI even
with characterization tests written, if those tests inherit the same
missing marker. Every new characterization test in §3 MUST carry
`pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit` (or `.integration` for CT-18) from the file
it's written in — call this out in review, don't rely on remembering it.

**Step 1 — extract `commands.py` first.** Gated by: nothing new (CT's not
needed — §3.8 confirms this cluster is already covered). This is the
lowest-risk extraction and validates the move mechanics (import updates,
facade re-exports) on a cluster where a mistake is guaranteed to be caught
by tests that already exist and already pass. Do this first so any
tooling/process mistake in "how we do a move" surfaces here, not on a
cluster that's currently unguarded.

**Step 2 — write CT-12 through CT-19 (prompt pipeline), THEN extract
`prompts.py`.** Gated by: CT-12-CT-18 passing against the CURRENT file
location, before any file is moved. Delete the `test_cc_command_features.py`
decoy (CT-19) in the SAME PR as the extraction, not before — deleting it
earlier would leave the interim state with less visible coverage than
before, even though the decoy provided none; deleting it in the same PR
that adds real coverage keeps the diff legible as a net improvement, not a
net removal. This step is prioritized second (right after the safe one)
because the gate report calls it the single highest-priority item to
characterize given blast radius.

**Step 3 — write CT-1 through CT-9 (dedup/ledger/pending-SHA trio), THEN
extract `dedup.py`.** Gated by: CT-1-CT-9 passing pre-move. This cluster is
the largest by uncovered-line-count and the most repetitive-looking (three
near-identical Postgres/Redis/in-memory/raise shapes), which per §2 is
exactly what invites an over-eager consolidation during the move — the
tests exist specifically to make that consolidation fail loudly if it
changes behavior. If the optional TDD settings-injection from §4 is taken,
do it INSIDE this step (write the injection test, change the signature,
confirm CT-1–CT-9 still pass unmodified against the new signature), not as
a separate step — splitting it out risks landing the signature change
without the characterization net still attached.

**Step 4 — write CT-10, CT-11 (controller), THEN extract `execution.py`.**
Gated by: CT-10-CT-11, plus CT-23-CT-24 (`_build_session_store`, same target
module) passing pre-move. `execution.py` is the module that WIRES the
dedup/prompt/controller collaborators together
(`get_execution_processor` calls `_create_import_ledger()`,
`_build_workspace_prompt`, `get_controller()`, `_build_session_store()`
directly) — sequencing it after steps 2 and 3 means its dependencies are
already extracted and independently tested by the time this step touches
the function that wires them, so a wiring mistake here shows up as "this
one function's assembly is wrong," not "which of five things I moved at
once broke."

**Step 5 — write CT-20, CT-21, CT-22 (singleton reset contracts), THEN
extract `claude_plugins.py` and `skills.py` together (or claude_plugins
first, skills second — they don't depend on each other).** Gated by: CT-20-CT-22
passing pre-move, run against the CURRENT single-file module (this is
the one case in this plan where the test needs to run once before the split
to prove it CAN pass, and then immediately after to prove the split didn't
silently break `global` binding — see CT-20/21's own note that this is only
observable post-extraction against real module namespaces). This is last
because it's the most mechanically fiddly (nine + four `global` statements
whose correctness depends on staying in the same file as their reset
function) and benefits from every other cluster already being out of the
file, shrinking the diff to just this concern.

**Step 6 — everything left in the remainder module.** No new
characterization tests gated per §3.9 (residual risk only, documented
inline, not blocking). This step is last because it's what's left over once
every other cluster has its own module — confirms the remainder module is
actually small enough to be under the 750-line threshold without further
splitting.

A rough gate table, restating the above as "test IDs required green before
step N merges":

| Step | Extraction | Required green first |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `commands.py` | (existing tests, unchanged) |
| 2 | `prompts.py` | CT-12–CT-18 |
| 3 | `dedup.py` | CT-1–CT-9 |
| 4 | `execution.py` | CT-10, CT-11, CT-23, CT-24 |
| 5 | `claude_plugins.py`, `skills.py` | CT-20, CT-21, CT-22 |
| 6 | remainder | none new (§3.9) |

## 6. Summary for the reviewer

24 characterization tests (CT-1–CT-24, CT-19 is a deletion) covering the
three ADR-060 fallback trios, the full prompt-assembly pipeline, the
controller/session-store pair, and the singleton reset contracts — every
piece of §2's "most of the file by both line count and consequence" that
the gate found unpinned. One new TDD-able seam (optional settings
injection for the ADR-060 trio) and one contract test for the public import
surface. Six ordered steps, each independently mergeable, each leaving
`just qa-ci` green, sequenced so a cluster's tests exist before that
cluster moves and so the wiring-heavy `execution.py` step lands only after
what it wires has already been extracted and independently proven.
